column3: NKJV renders “Israel [is] a luxuriant vine” as “Israel empties his vine” (the Hebrew word can mean either), and “they made good” the pillars as “They have embellished.”
Close to the Hebrew; “their heart is slippery” is rendered “Their heart is divided.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the poisonous plant” is rendered “hemlock.”
NKJV renders “the heifers of Beth Aven” as singular, “the calf of Beth Aven,” and “its pagan priests … will tremble (or exult)” as “its priests shriek.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “The idol” as the subject, and renders “tribute” as “a present.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the high places of wickedness” is rendered as a name, “the high places of Aven.”
Close to the Hebrew; the question “will not war overtake them in Gibeah?” is rendered as a statement, “The battle in Gibeah … Did not overtake them.”
Close to the Hebrew; “their two iniquities” is rendered “their two transgressions.”
Close to the Hebrew; “I passed over the goodness of its neck” is rendered “I harnessed her fair neck,” and “will harrow” “shall break his clods.”
Close to the Hebrew; “reap to the mouth of loyalty” is rendered “Reap in mercy.”
Close to the Hebrew; “like the devastation of Shalman [at] Beth Arbel” is rendered “As Shalman plundered Beth Arbel.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the evil of your wickedness” is rendered “your great wickedness.”
